Identity: self and society

text: Read Source A and then answer the questions below.
In the United States Barbara Ehrenreich used covert participant observation to research how working
class people are able to live on low wages. For several months Ehrenreich left her middle-class
home and lived and worked with people in low-wage jobs. She found work in four different cities in
the United States. Her various jobs included being a waitress, a cleaner, a care home assistant
and a shop worker. She wrote down her experiences at the end of each day. For her research
Ehrenreich experienced trying to live on a low wage to pay for her food, clothing, transportation
Using covert participant observation allowed Ehrenreich to gain a first-hand, qualitative and in-depth
understanding of the difficult lives of low-wage workers. Her conclusions were:
• low-wage workers cannot afford basic necessities without working in more than one job
• low-wage workers are often socially controlled through random searches of their bags and
• managers had negative attitudes to low-wage workers based on class or racial prejudice
• medical treatment and childcare are too expensive for low-wage workers.
Source: adapted from an internet summary of ‘Nickel and Dimed’ by Barbara Ehrenreich.
